newsitem.title: USA: Schedule of major events for Clinton inauguration.
newsitem.headline: Schedule of major events for Clinton inauguration.

text.p: The swearing-in of President Bill Clinton for a second term will take only about 45 seconds on Monday but there are a host of official and unofficial events surrounding the inauguration.

It will be the 53rd inauguration of a president. Clinton will be the first president sworn in for a second term since Ronald Reagan in 1985 and the first Democrat elected to a second term since Franklin Roosevelt.
Following are highlights of the inauguration itself and the celebrations surrounding it. All times are approximate, EST/GMT.
7 a.m. (1200): Inaugural Prayer Breakfast. Clinton will join religious leaders at about 8 a.m. (1300) for prayers before the official inaugural events begin.
10:45 a.m. (1545): Escort to the Capitol. Congressional leaders escort Clinton and Vice President Al Gore in a motorcade from the White House to the Capitol.

11:30 a.m. (1630): Inauguration Ceremony. Supreme Court Chief Justice William Rehnquist administers the oath of office to Clinton and Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg swears-in Vice President Al Gore at the West Front of the Capitol.
12:05 p.m. (1705): Inaugural address. Clinton delivers his inaugural address from the West Front of the Capitol.

12:50 p.m. (1750): Luncheon. Clinton, Gore and their families lunch with congressional leaders, Supreme Court justices and Cabinet members in Statuary Hall, the former House chamber on the second floor of the Capitol.

2 p.m. (1900): Inaugural Parade. Clinton, Gore and their families lead parade from the Capitol down Pennsylvania Avenue to the White House. The parade features representatives from all 50 states, the District of Columbia and U.S. territories and includes marching bands, equestrian groups and floats.

7 p.m. (Midnight): Official Inaugural balls. Tuxedos and taffeta will dominate at elegant balls held around Washington. Clinton, first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton and the Gores will make a whirlwind tour of all 14 official black-tie events attended by some 75,000 people.
There will be a host of other events including:

7:30 p.m. (0030): Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., Memorial Concert. The Washington National Cathedral, an immense church that dominates the capital skyline, is turned into a concert hall for a musical presentation to honour the slain civil rights leader. The inauguration coincides with the holiday to commemorate King's birthday.

10:30 a.m. (1530): "An American Journey: Building a Bridge to the 21st Century." A two-day celebration with free events, concerts, a musical, food, speeches and fireworks begins in huge, heated tents set up on the Mall.
9 p.m. (0200): MTV/Conde Nast party. One of the most sought-after invitations in Washington is to the cocktail party hosted by Music Television.

5 p.m. (2200): Inaugural Gala. Clinton and first lady join about 11,000 people who have paid as much as $3,000 each for tickets to a gala celebration at USAir Arena. Performers include Gloria Estefan, Mikhail Baryshnikov, Aretha Franklin, Whoopi Goldberg, Dave Matthews Band, Kenny G, Bernadette Peters, Kenny Rogers, James Taylor and Stevie Wonder.
